items.title: We have $8 million in traditional IRAs. Should we tap them to buy a house — and take the tax hit?
items.description: “We would rather pay taxes upfront than pay mortgage interest.”

items.title: The S&P 500’s earnings growth has gone bonkers thanks to one company
items.description: Markets are gearing up for the busiest week of second-quarter earnings season.

items.title: ‘We are not romantically involved’: I’m marrying my platonic best friend of 20 years. Should I leave him my home?
items.description: “I own my home outright, have no children or other dependents.”

items.title: There’s a technical ‘triple threat’ for stocks, but also places investors can hide
items.description: Treasury yields and oil prices surged, and the dollar confirmed the breakout toward a longer-term uptrend, to push the S&P 500 below key chart support.

items.title: I will definitely claim Social Security early. Why do so few people talk about the elephant in the room?
items.description: “The strongest argument for claiming benefits earlier goes beyond the traditional break-even analyses.”

items.title: The Treasury market is sending Fed Chair Kevin Warsh a clear warning about rates
items.description: Rising Treasury yields show how “enormously worried” the market is about inflation — and whether the Fed will back up its tough talk with action

items.title: ‘I’m still confused’: I sold $80,000 in shares on June 30, so why didn’t I receive my dividend?
items.description: “To my surprise, the proceeds from the sale were credited to my money-market settlement fund.”

items.title: ‘Time will tell whether that was a good bet’: My adviser got me a full SpaceX IPO allocation. Was I lucky?
items.description: “Investors frequently receive only a small fraction of the shares they request — if they receive any at all.”

items.title: I want to transfer $17,000 in credit-card debt. Why did Wells Fargo offer me only a $4,000 credit limit?
items.description: “I asked why the limit was so low, but they couldn’t give me an explanation.”

items.title: I am a 63-year-old semiretired physician. If I saved $2 million for retirement, should my Social Security become optional?
items.description: “At that point, they arguably no longer need the government’s retirement safety net.”
